title: Finite closed-point complement of a dense open in a curve
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a curve [def-sc-curves], and $V\subseteq C$ a dense open. Then $C\setminus V$ is finite, each of its points is closed [def-weil-closed-points], and each residue field [def-weil-residue-field] is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]. No reducedness, irreducibility, smoothness or properness is assumed.

proof.text: Finite type and quasi-compactness make C Noetherian. For an irreducible component Z remove the other finitely many components to obtain an open W with closure Z (Mathlib closure_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff_singleton). Thus W is nonempty and density gives a point of V in Z. The irreducible subspace Z has dimension at most one by the subspace dimension inequality. Apply the dimension-one closed-point lemma to the nonempty open V intersect Z: each point of Z outside V is closed in Z, hence in C. For each x outside V take Z to be a component containing x.

Decompose the closed complement into finitely many closed irreducible subsets using NoetherianSpace.exists_finite_set_isClosed_irreducible. Sobriety supplies a generic point z of each. This z lies outside V and so is closed by the first step. The subset, equal to the closure of z, is a singleton. A finite union of these singletons is finite. Lean proves this directly, without the unproved finite_of_isClosed_of_closed_points theorem.

Use residueFieldIsoBase f x (hcl x hx) for each point outside V. Transport algebraic closedness of k across its inverse ring equivalence, then infer separable closedness. Empty curves and empty complements are included.

lean.statement:
theorem dense_open_finite_complement {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f]
    (V : C.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set C)) :
    (V : Set C)ᶜ.Finite ∧ (∀ x ∉ V, IsClosed ({x} : Set C)) ∧
      (∀ x ∉ V, IsSepClosed (C.residueField x))
